title: Law-by-law assembly of disp_Monad_laws_from_hss, the monad laws of the monad induced by a heterogeneous substitution system
intent: Reduces the monad laws of the monad induced by a heterogeneous substitution system (hss) to four same-file lemmas: the two unit laws are closed by named lemmas, and the associativity law is closed not by a single named lemma but by a transitivity bridge (intermediate_path) between two named equations for the bracket μ_3.

children.name: Monad_law_1_from_hss
children.statement:
Lemma Monad_law_1_from_hss :
  ∏ c : C, μ_0 (pr1 (`T) c) · μ_2 c = identity ((pr1 (`T)) c).
children.closed_by: apply pathsinv0. apply H2 (with H' := prejoin_from_hetsubst_η T)
children.note: First unit law η · μ = id; the proof unfolds μ_0 and applies the η-law of the prejoin.

children.name: Monad_law_2_from_hss
children.statement:
Lemma Monad_law_2_from_hss:
  ∏ c : C, # (pr1 (`T)) (μ_0 c)· μ_2 c = identity ((pr1 (`T)) c).
children.closed_by: apply μ_1_identity' (right branch of intermediate_path (μ_1 c))
children.note: Second unit law Tη · μ = id; the proof goes through μ_1 and the uniqueness of the bracket, closing the right side with the same-file sibling μ_1_identity'.

children.name: μ_3_T_μ_2_μ_2
children.note: Left associativity equation μ_3 = (T ∘ μ_2) · μ_2, by uniqueness of the bracket; reuses Monad_law_1_from_hss as a leaf (line 300).

children.name: μ_3_μ_2_T_μ_2
children.statement:
Lemma μ_3_μ_2_T_μ_2 :  (
    @compose (functor_category C C)
                 (* TtimesTthenT *) T²∙T _ _
                 (* (@functor_composite C C C ((functor_ptd_forget C hs) T)
                    ((functor_ptd_forget C hs) T))
                 ((functor_ptd_forget C hs) T) *)
          ((μ_2 •• `T) (* :  TtimesTthenT' --> _ *)
                  (*:@functor_compose C C C hs hs
                    (@functor_composite C C C ((functor_ptd_forget C hs) T)
                                              ((functor_ptd_forget C hs) T))
                    ((functor_ptd_forget C hs) T) --> _*) ) μ_2 :
            (*TtimesTthenT'*) T•T² --> `T) = μ_3.
children.note: Right associativity equation (μ_2 •• T) · μ_2 = μ_3, by uniqueness of the bracket; reuses Monad_law_1_from_hss as a leaf (line 368).

applicability.goal_shape: A goal that is a structure/record of laws (here disp_Monad_laws over disp_Monad_data_from_hss) whose fields are equations; the glue split-s the record and closes each field with a named lemma, and one field is an equality proved by showing both sides equal to a common intermediate value via intermediate_path.
applicability.use_when: Each field of the structure has a separately proved lemma in the same development, and an equality field can be closed by a transitivity (calc) chain whose links are named equations to a shared intermediate object (here the bracket μ_3).
applicability.avoid_when: A single named lemma for the whole law would be shorter and clearer; the two sides of the equality are equal to different representatives, so the intermediate_path bridge does not typecheck; or the record's fields are trivial enough for one automation pass.

metrics.how_counted: Lines of the five sites in the copied file (declaration plus proof); no child closes by a single automation tactic — each closes by applying a named project lemma (apply H2 / apply μ_1_identity' / apply (fbracket_unique T μ_2_ptd)).

consequences: The glue splits disp_Monad_laws into its two components, then the associativity component is closed by a transitivity bridge rather than one lemma: both μ_3 equations must land on the same intermediate value (μ_3) for intermediate_path to typecheck, and each is flipped by pathsinv0 because the named equations are oriented μ_3 = …, while the goal wants the reverse orientation. Failure mode: if the two sides of the associative law are equal to different representatives of μ_3, the bridge does not apply and the law needs a single named lemma, or an explicit associator as in the file's third_monad_law_from_hss (which inserts rassociator_CAT).
